abstract.t: This document specifies the HTTP Mail Transfer Protocol (HMTP), a protocol for the submission and transfer of Internet mail over HTTPS. HMTP retains what SMTP and the mail system built around it have proven, namely the Internet Message Format, the separation of envelope and message, and the semantics of delivery and delivery status notifications, and adds what SMTP provides only through optional extensions or not at all. Security is built in: transport encryption is mandatory, and every transfer request is signed on behalf of the sending domain, using keys published with the DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) key publication mechanism. Requests carry identifiers that make retries safe, failures are reported per recipient as structured problem details with a mapping to SMTP status codes, and extensions are declared explicitly as capabilities. Messages are carried unmodified inside a JSON envelope, and large messages and attachments can be transferred by reference, with their integrity protected by cryptographic hashes. Servers discover HMTP endpoints through DNS and a well-known URI, and a domain can publish a policy that prevents downgrade to SMTP. HMTP does not depend on SMTP, but an implementation can optionally fall back to SMTP when a peer does not support HMTP, so that it can be deployed incrementally alongside existing systems.
